newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets on Monday were inactive, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Bids were light and scattered at $68.00 and passed by owners asking mostly $70.00, with a few at $71.00.
Fed cattle prices this week were seen underpinned by projections for smaller numbers of market-ready cattle on showlists, compared with last week, they said.
Avverage weights last week were four lbs below the previous week, reflecting aggressive packer buying which kept feedlots current in their marketings, sources said.
Showlists this week were estimated near 84,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, down 1,800 from the previous week, market sources said.
Kansas showlists were pegged near 91,000 head, up about 8,000 from last week, but much of the increase came from lightweight cattle, they said.

Nebraska's showlist was estimated near 85,000 head, up about 2,000. Bids in Nebraska on Monday were light from $109.00 to $110.00 per cwt on a dressed basis and passed by owners pricing $112.00, sources there said.
